name: The Sudd (Ramsar wetland)
blurb: A vast White Nile swamp where floods feed grasses, fish, birds and antelope.

tip.title: Shrink the flood
tip.text: The White Nile flood spreads over the plain each year. Lower White Nile flood pulse by 50% and watch the floodplain grasses, then lechwe, kob, hippos and crocodiles.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: White Nile flood pulse
nodes.desc: Water from upstream spreads across the flat clay plain each wet season, flooding the swamp and shrinking back in the dry season. It sets which plants grow where.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong tropical light drives rapid growth of floodplain grasses, papyrus and algae in the shallow water.

nodes.name: Dry-season fire
nodes.desc: Floodplain grasses stand tall in the rains and are often burned in the dry season, renewing grazing for wildlife and livestock.

nodes.name: Clay floodplain soil
nodes.desc: Heavy, poorly draining clays hold floodwater and trap sediment and nutrients that feed the swamp plants.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Bacteria and fungi break down dead swamp vegetation and carcasses, returning nutrients to the water and soil.

nodes.name: Papyrus
nodes.desc: A tall sedge forming dense stands and floating mats in the Sudd, shaping habitat for birds such as the shoebill.

nodes.name: Hippo grass
nodes.desc: A robust floodplain grass of the Sudd that grows in deeper water and is a main swamp plant.

nodes.name: Wild millet grasses
nodes.desc: Floodplain grasses that spread over the semi-flooded plains as water rises, forming rich seasonal pasture.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Microscopic algae in the open water and channels, grazed by fish and small animals.

nodes.name: Nile lechwe
nodes.desc: An endangered, semi-aquatic antelope of the Sudd floodplains that grazes marsh vegetation in shallow water.

nodes.name: White-eared kob
nodes.desc: A grazing antelope whose huge seasonal herds migrate across the grasslands of South Sudan.

nodes.name: Tiang
nodes.desc: A grazing antelope that migrates with kob and gazelle across South Sudan plains.

nodes.name: Hippopotamus
nodes.desc: Spends the day in water and grazes grasses on land at night; it lives in the Sudd shallows.

nodes.name: Nile tilapia
nodes.desc: A common fish of the Sudd that feeds largely on algae and plant material, and is prey for many larger animals.

nodes.name: Black crowned crane
nodes.desc: A wetland crane that feeds on seeds, insects and small animals in grasslands and shallow water of the Sudd.

nodes.name: Marbled lungfish
nodes.desc: An air-breathing fish of swamps that eats fish and molluscs; it is a key prey of the shoebill.

nodes.name: Elongate tigerfish
nodes.desc: A fast predatory fish recorded in the Sudd system that hunts smaller fish.

nodes.name: Shoebill
nodes.desc: A giant wading bird for which the Sudd is a major stronghold; it hunts large fish such as lungfish in papyrus swamp.

nodes.name: Great white pelican
nodes.desc: A large fish-eating waterbird that uses the Sudd and its channels.

nodes.name: African fish eagle
nodes.desc: A fish-eating eagle of African lakes and rivers that takes fish from the surface of open water.

nodes.name: Hooded vulture
nodes.desc: A small scavenging vulture recorded near the Sudd that feeds on carcasses and scraps.

nodes.name: Nile crocodile
nodes.desc: A top predator of the swamp that eats fish and ambushes antelope at the water edge.

nodes.name: Lion
nodes.desc: A top predator of South Sudan savannas that hunts grazing antelope such as kob and tiang.
